title: metrics.stats (and call_logs.model_alias) keyed by the unresolved, length-unbounded client model string -> permanent unbounded growth
verified_cites: backend/internal/metrics/metrics.go:56-71 Observe; 60 `s := mt.stats[model]`; 63 `mt.stats[model] = s` (verbatim, verbatim) — sole writer besides New() at 53; no delete/cap/TTL/reset anywhere in the 124-line file
backend/internal/metrics/metrics.go:88-103 QPS() rotates+copies but never prunes (dead keys already report QPS 0 at line 99, so eviction there is loss-free)
backend/internal/metrics/metrics.go:58-59 Observe holds mt.mu for its whole body

backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go:195 MaxConnections (concurrency only), 215-221 key validity, 222-227 IP allowlist — no per-IP/per-key request-rate throttle; backend/cmd/server/main.go:95-118 registers only Recovery/headers/access-log
reason: CONFIRMED at high. Every quoted line was read end-to-end and matches verbatim at the cited numbers; the chain holds with no mitigating control in the flow. metrics.go:63 permanently inserts an entry for whatever string Observe is handed and nothing in the package ever deletes it (repo-wide grep for delete/mt.stats confirms the only delete is hub.go:41 subscribers and slb.go:215 inner cursors). Handle registers the observation in a defer (gateway.go:314) whose key is assigned at 334 from the raw client model, before any of the three resolution attempts (335, 339-346, 351-354), and the unknown-model rejection returns at 356-361 — strictly before the API-key model allowlist (370), guard (381-407), rate limiter (410) and quota (419). So an authenticated caller with a key restricted to one model, or with quota exhausted, can still mint arbitrary map entries, and the request is answered with a 404 in microseconds without any counter being consulted. There is no global limiter in the middleware chain (AuthMiddleware 189-231 checks only concurrency/key/IP; main.go 95-118 adds nothing). The string is never length- or charset-validated on any of the three parse paths (adapter.go:120/212/316 test only emptiness), and with the 16 MiB inbound cap (gateway.go:322) one retained key may itself be ~16 MiB — so both key count and key length are unbounded, exactly as filed. The same string is also persisted per rejected request (gateway.go:273 into model.go:253, an indexed column that SQLite does not length-enforce; call audit defaults on at settings.go:33 and status != ok bypasses the only-errors/sampling filters at gateway.go:257-259), and it is re-emitted to any caller on every scrape (prom.go:136-138, /metrics unauthenticated per routes.go:19-24). One verified consequence that strengthens the finding beyond the filed text: because Observe holds mt.mu (metrics.go:58) and QPS() holds the same mutex across the whole map iteration (metrics.go:89-100) reached from the unauthenticated scrape via admin/prom.go:15 under promMu (prom.go:113), the attacker-minted entry count converts into key-count-proportional blocking of every legitimate gateway request — a restart-only amplification of an unauthenticated path, not merely a leak. Imprecisions found, none load-bearing: (a) disk growth is not permanent — audit.go:88-106 cleanupLoop prunes CallLog rows older than AuditRetentionDays (default 90) hourly and call audit can be switched off (settings.go:25), so 'cannot be mitigated by configuration' is true only for the memory half (which has no bound or config at all, and disabling audit actually accelerates it by removing the synchronous-insert backpressure at audit.go:44); (b) under DB_TYPE=mysql/postgres size:64 maps to VARCHAR(64) and the oversized row insert fails and is dropped at audit.go:67-69, making the megabyte-indexed-row consequence SQLite-default-specific, while mt.stats growth is dialect-independent; (c) slb.go:213-217 prunes the inner provider-cursor map, not the outer bl.rr alias keys — still a fair precedent for the recommendation, and bl.rr keys are config-derived; (d) ModelStat payload is 960 B (two [60]int64) + 8 B lastSec = 968 B plus the key string; (e) the PoC must send "messages":[] on /v1/chat/completions (with the field absent, adapter.go:136-138 fails -> 400 and ap.alias is never assigned), which is what the filed PoC does; /v1/messages is even cheaper (Messages is a plain slice, adapter.go:302-305). Severity: high is correct — attacker needs only one valid gateway key, the effect is irreversible for the process lifetime and kills the single process serving gateway + admin + SPA (OOM), so it is authed-but-severe rather than an unauth critical. Line refinement only: cited 60 is the map read; the permanent insertion is 63.
impact: Any holder of one enabled gateway API key can permanently grow an in-process, never-pruned map with attacker-chosen names of attacker-chosen length (up to ~16 MiB per key), unthrottled and unchecked by the model allowlist, guard, rate limiter or quota because the 404 return at gateway.go:356-361 precedes all of them. Memory is a monotonic high-water mark for the life of the process: ~1 KB per short name (200k names ~ 300 MB) or ~64 requests per retained GB using 16 MiB names. Each rejected request also writes a call_logs row carrying the full string in an indexed column (bounded only by AuditRetentionDays, default 90 days, or by disabling call audit). Retention is then re-serialized on every unauthenticated /metrics scrape and on every authenticated /status view, and because Observe/QPS share mt.mu, the attacker-chosen entry count also translates into blocked authenticated gateway requests driven by unauthenticated /metrics polling. Terminal state: OOM of the single process (gateway + admin API + SPA all die together), or SQLite file/index bloat degrading every audit and token-statistics query. No configuration mitigates the memory half, and recovery requires a restart.
exploit_sketch: Prerequisite: one valid enabled sk- key (no model permission or quota headroom needed). (1) Mint keys unthrottled: `for i in $(seq 1 200000); do curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST http://target:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<valid>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"zz-'$i'","messages":[]}'; done` -> each request misses at gateway.go:335/351, returns 404 at 356-361 before allowlist/limiter/quota, and the defer at 314-319 permanently adds one entry via metrics.go:60-64. (2) Fast variant: N distinct requests whose model field is a unique ~16 MiB string (gateway.go:322 cap) -> ~64 requests retain ~1 GiB. (3) Weaponize the retained set from an unauthenticated socket: `while :; do curl -s http://target:8080/metrics >/dev/null; done` -> each scrape scans all N entries holding mt.mu (metrics.go:89-100 via admin/prom.go:15), stalling every legitimate request in Observe (gateway.go:318), while the response body itself grows without bound (prom.go:135-139). Nothing recovers short of a process restart.
recommendation: (1) Validate the client model string in adapter.ParseRequest for all three protocols (reject >128 bytes, and non `[A-Za-z0-9._:/\[\]-]`) so no downstream consumer (stats map, call_logs, Prometheus label, 404 body echo) ever sees an unbounded token. (2) Do not observe unresolved names: move `s.mx.Observe(...)` out of the pre-resolution defer to after resolution and use the resolved alias, or bucket every pre-resolution rejection under one fixed key (e.g. `__unknown__`) — this also removes the unthrottled-path growth without losing error visibility. (3) Bound the map regardless: cap `len(mt.stats)` (e.g. 1024, folding overflow into `__other__`) and delete entries with `lastSec` older than ~60s inside the existing QPS() sweep (metrics.go:92-100), which is loss-free since stale entries already report 0 QPS. (4) Truncate/clamp ap.alias and ap.errMsg to a fixed length before writeLog (gateway.go:273/357) so indexed call_logs columns stay within their declared size on every dialect.
mitigations_checked: Inbound 16 MiB body cap (gateway.go:322) bounds one key's size per request but neither the count nor cumulative retention; gateway auth required (gateway.go:215-221) so the attacker needs one valid key; MaxConnections (gateway.go:195) bounds concurrency, not the cumulative key set; gin middleware chain (main.go:95-118) contains no rate limiter and AuthMiddleware (189-231) no per-key/IP request-rate cap; ErrorEvent ring IS bounded (metrics.go:77-79) so this is an inconsistency, not a package-wide policy; slb.go:213-217 prunes inner rr cursors (outer bl.rr alias keys are config-derived and safe); call_logs retention pruner exists (audit.go:88-106, default 90 days) and bounds the disk half but not memory; DB dialects other than SQLite would reject/truncate the oversized indexed column (audit.go:67-69 drops the batch on error); model allowlist (370), guard (381-407), limiter (410) and quota (419) all run after the 404 return and therefore provide no protection on this path; /metrics unauthenticated by design (routes.go:19-24).
